news.title: AI Agents Are Transforming How Software Is Built
news.content:
Artificial intelligence agents are rapidly changing the way software developers write and maintain code. Major technology companies including Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI have released AI-powered coding assistants that can understand complex programming tasks and generate working code in minutes.

These AI agents go beyond simple code completion. They can analyze entire codebases, identify bugs, suggest architectural improvements, and even write unit tests automatically. Developers report that using these tools has increased their productivity by 30 to 50 percent on routine tasks.

The technology works by combining large language models with specialized reasoning capabilities. When a developer describes a feature in natural language, the AI agent breaks the request into smaller steps, searches through existing code for relevant patterns, and generates a complete implementation. It can also explain its reasoning, making it easier for developers to review and modify the output.

However, the rise of AI coding tools has sparked debate in the software industry. Some experienced developers worry that junior programmers may become overly dependent on AI assistance, potentially weakening their fundamental coding skills. Others argue that these tools free developers to focus on higher-level design and problem-solving rather than repetitive boilerplate code.

Companies are also grappling with security and intellectual property concerns. AI-generated code may inadvertently include copyrighted snippets or introduce subtle vulnerabilities that human reviewers might miss. As a result, many organizations are implementing policies that require thorough code review even for AI-generated contributions.

Despite these challenges, adoption continues to accelerate. A recent survey found that over 70 percent of professional developers now use some form of AI coding assistant in their daily work. Industry analysts predict that within the next two years, AI agents will be involved in the majority of software development activities worldwide.

sentences.original: These AI agents go beyond simple code completion.
sentences.translation: 这些AI智能体超越了简单的代码补全功能。
sentences.structure: 主语(These AI agents) + 谓语(go beyond) + 宾语(simple code completion)。go beyond 意为「超越，不止于」，是一个常用的动词短语。

sentences.original: When a developer describes a feature in natural language, the AI agent breaks the request into smaller steps.
sentences.translation: 当开发者用自然语言描述一个功能时，AI智能体会将请求分解为更小的步骤。
sentences.structure: 时间状语从句(When...language) + 主句(the AI agent...steps)。break...into... 意为「把……分解为……」，是高频搭配。

sentences.original: Others argue that these tools free developers to focus on higher-level design and problem-solving.
sentences.translation: 另一些人则认为，这些工具让开发者得以专注于更高层次的设计和问题解决。
sentences.structure: 主语(Others) + 谓语(argue) + that宾语从句。free sb to do sth 意为「使某人得以做某事」，focus on 意为「专注于」。

sentences.original: AI-generated code may inadvertently include copyrighted snippets or introduce subtle vulnerabilities that human reviewers might miss.
sentences.translation: AI生成的代码可能会无意中包含受版权保护的代码片段，或者引入人类审查者可能遗漏的微妙漏洞。
sentences.structure: 主语(AI-generated code) + 谓语(may include...or introduce) + 并列宾语(copyrighted snippets / subtle vulnerabilities) + that定语从句修饰vulnerabilities。这是一个较长的复合句，注意 may 表示可能性。

sentences.original: Industry analysts predict that within the next two years, AI agents will be involved in the majority of software development activities worldwide.
sentences.translation: 行业分析师预测，在未来两年内，AI智能体将参与到全球大多数软件开发活动中。
sentences.structure: 主语(Industry analysts) + 谓语(predict) + that宾语从句。从句中 within the next two years 是时间状语，be involved in 意为「参与，涉及」。
